title: The landed rollback is hardened: previous image redeployed without rebuild, atomic order proven by mutation, recovery proven through the real probe
description:
SPIDR successor of task-95e68a8dd2464e7b8ad4b1f8c4d2b2e4, cut by architect-b63fabf3 on 2026-09-05. That row carried backups, a new human-only command kind and this effect; the kind alone is a two-row roster job on this board, so the three were separated. This row is the EFFECT: it owns the parent's DoD 5, 6 and 7.

dependsOn: task-b22462cf (the wired kind, whose fail-closed stub this row replaces), task-95e68a8d (the backups this row optionally restores from), and task-6ec875f4 (the probe that confirms recovery).

WHAT THIS ROW OWNS: `deployment.rollback {environment, toReceiptRef}` actually rolling back - resolving the previous image from the KEPT DEPLOY RECEIPT, redeploying it with the same atomic replace and health probe the forward deploy uses, restoring the database backup ONLY when explicitly requested, and confirming recovery through the real probe.

NEVER REBUILD AN IMAGE TO SATISFY A ROLLBACK. This is the row's hardest rule and the one most likely to be softened under pressure: a rebuild from source under the same sha produces a DIFFERENT image, so an environment "rolled back" that way is running bytes nobody has ever run. When the receipt names an image that no longer exists locally, the honest answer is `ROLLBACK_IMAGE_MISSING` - a refusal, not a rebuild.

THE RECEIPT SHAPE IS A SIBLING'S, NOT THIS ROW'S. task-c0e00f0a (the deploy engine) stores the kept deploy receipt and its completion record is required to NAME the retrieval call for exactly this reason - that row is a sibling and cannot be depended on, so read its completionSummary and build against what actually shipped rather than what was designed.

REUSE THE FORWARD DEPLOY'S ATOMIC REPLACE. A rollback that replaces differently from a deploy is a second lifecycle to reason about during an incident, which is precisely when nobody has the patience for two. The switch point, the health probe and the teardown all come from the deploy engine.

NOT IN SCOPE: the backups themselves (task-95e68a8d), the command kind's roster and fence (task-37a50989 and task-b22462cf), the probe (task-6ec875f4), and the incident card UI (task-f008f29a).

VERIFY: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`.
